lessons.title: Set of zeroes of a polynomial function

objectives.label: Define set of zeroes
objectives.description: Evaluate a polynomial function at given values of x and state the set of zeroes Z(f) as the values of x for which f(x)=0.

objectives.label: Find set of zeroes
objectives.description: Find the set of zeroes Z(f) of a polynomial function by putting f(x) = 0 and solving the resulting equation for x, including cases with no zeroes.

entries.text: 0, 1 and 2 are called the set of zeroes of the function.

A.why: It names 0, 1 and 2 as the set of zeroes after evaluating the activity's f(x), defining the term.

B.why: Names 0, 1 and 2 as the set of zeroes after evaluating the activity's f(x), which defines the term.

entries.text: Z(f) is the solution set of the equation f(x) = 0. $f(x)=0$

A.why: It states Z(f) is the solution set of f(x)=0, the method used for finding zeroes by solving the equation.

B.why: States that Z(f) is the solution set of f(x)=0, the method for finding zeroes by solving the equation.

objectives.label: Domain of algebraic fraction
objectives.description: Determine the domain of an algebraic fractional function as R minus the set of zeroes of the denominator, and evaluate the function at given values.

objectives.label: Common domain of fractions
objectives.description: Calculate the common domain of two or more algebraic fractions as R minus the union of the zeroes of their denominators.

entries.text: The rational number in the form $\frac{a}{b}$ where $a, b \in Z$, $b \neq 0$. Given $p: R \to R$, $p(x) = x + 3$ and $f: R \to R$, $f(x) = x^2 - 4$.

A.why: Recalls rational numbers and sets up p and f as assumed background, not taught here.

B.why: Recalls rational numbers and sets up p and f, assumed background.

entries.text: n, where $n(x) = \frac{x+3}{x^2-4}$, is called an algebraic fractional function or an algebraic fraction. $n(x) = \frac{x + 3}{x^2 - 4}$

A.why: Introduces the idea of an algebraic fraction for the whole lesson before domains are treated.

B.why: Names the example function as an algebraic fraction, introducing the lesson.

entries.text: The domain is R except for the values of x which make the fraction undefined (the set of zeroes of the denominator).

A.why: States the domain as R except where the denominator's zeroes make the fraction undefined.

B.why: States the domain is R except where the denominator is zero.

entries.text: The domain of n(x) is R - {-2, 2}. $R - \{-2, 2\}$

A.why: Shows the domain of n(x) as R - {-2, 2}, the zeroes of the denominator.

B.why: Gives the domain of n(x) as R - {-2, 2} for the example fraction.

entries.text: If p and f are two polynomial functions and z(f) is the set of zeroes of f, then the function n: R - z(f) → R, n(x) = p(x)/f(x) is called a real algebraic fractional function, or briefly an algebraic fraction. $n: R - z(f) \to R,\ n(x) = \frac{p(x)}{f(x)}$

A.why: Defines the fraction on R - z(f), the domain excluding zeroes of the denominator.

B.why: Defines an algebraic fraction, general introduction to the lesson's concept.

entries.text: The common domain of two or more algebraic fractions is the set of real numbers where the fractions are identified together completely (at the same time).

A.why: Defines the common domain of two or more algebraic fractions.

B.why: Defines the common domain of two or more fractions.

entries.text: The common domain of a number of algebraic fractions = R - the set of zeroes of the denominators of these fractions.

A.why: States the common domain as R minus the zeroes of all the denominators.

B.why: States common domain as R minus the zeroes of the denominators.

objectives.label: Reducing algebraic fractions with domain
objectives.description: Reduce an algebraic fraction to its simplest form by factorizing numerator and denominator, and state its domain before cancelling common factors.

objectives.label: Equality of two algebraic fractions
objectives.description: Determine whether two algebraic fractions are equal by comparing their domains and their simplest forms, and find the common domain when they are not equal.

entries.text: Step 3: remove the common factor in both the numerator and denominator to get the simplest form.

A.why: Step 3 of reducing a fraction: cancel the common factor to get the simplest form.

B.why: Step of the reducing method: remove the common factor to get the simplest form.

entries.text: An algebraic fraction is in its simplest form if there are no common factors between its numerator and denominator.

A.why: Defines simplest form (no common factors), which is what reducing fractions produces.

B.why: Defines the simplest form of an algebraic fraction, which is what reducing by factorizing and cancelling aims at.

objectives.label: Add and subtract algebraic fractions
objectives.description: Add and subtract algebraic fractions with common or different denominators, factorising denominators, using the L.C.M., giving the result in simplest form with its domain.

objectives.label: Multiply and divide algebraic fractions
objectives.description: Multiply and divide algebraic fractions by factorising and cancelling, dividing by multiplying by the multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of the second, giving the simplest form and the domain.

entries.text: For two algebraic fractions with a common denominator, n1(x)=f1(x)/f2(x), n2(x)=f3(x)/f2(x): the sum is (f1(x)+f3(x))/f2(x). $n_1(x)+n_2(x)=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}+\frac{f_3(x)}{f_2(x)}=\frac{f_1(x)+f_3(x)}{f_2(x)}$

A.why: Rule for adding algebraic fractions with a common denominator.

B.why: Rule for adding fractions with a common denominator.

entries.text: With a common denominator, the difference is (f1(x) - f3(x))/f2(x), also written as f1(x)/f2(x) + (-f3(x))/f2(x). $n_1(x)-n_2(x)=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}-\frac{f_3(x)}{f_2(x)}=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}+\frac{-f_3(x)}{f_2(x)}$

A.why: Rule for subtracting algebraic fractions with a common denominator.

B.why: Rule for subtracting fractions with a common denominator.

entries.text: For two algebraic fractions with different denominators, n1(x)=f1(x)/f2(x), n2(x)=f3(x)/f4(x): the sum is (f1(x)×f4(x)+f3(x)×f2(x))/(f2(x)×f4(x)). $n_1(x)+n_2(x)=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}+\frac{f_3(x)}{f_4(x)}=\frac{f_1(x)\times f_4(x)+f_3(x)\times f_2(x)}{f_2(x)\times f_4(x)}$

A.why: Rule for adding algebraic fractions with different denominators.

B.why: Rule for adding fractions with different denominators.

entries.text: With different denominators, the difference is (f1(x)×f4(x) - f3(x)×f2(x))/(f2(x)×f4(x)). $n_1(x)-n_2(x)=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}-\frac{f_3(x)}{f_4(x)}=\frac{f_1(x)\times f_4(x)-f_3(x)\times f_2(x)}{f_2(x)\times f_4(x)}$

A.why: Rule for subtracting algebraic fractions with different denominators.

B.why: Rule for subtracting fractions with different denominators.
